pageTitle: 3DS Personal Website · Make a familiar place your own
metaDescription: Create your own personal website with a Nintendo 3DS-inspired interface. Explore the demo, customize your profile and pages, and install with the local setup wizard.
heroDescription: A personal website with the warmth of the Nintendo 3DS settings menu. Your profile, your pages, your little corner of the internet.
heroNote: Free software. Local setup. Yours to personalize.
previewNote: A real screen from the independent demo.
featuresTitle:
A familiar menu.
A place that feels like you.
featuresIntro: Keep the raised buttons and gentle transitions. Fill the rest with what matters to you.
tour.profile.title: More than a username.
tour.profile.description: Start with a photo and your name. Add a little introduction or a longer biography when you have more to say.
tour.profile.point3: Social links and your own icons
tour.sona.title: Room for the rest of your world.
tour.sona.description: Create a Sona sheet, share a gallery, collect links or show your projects. Each page can have its own title, images and artist credits.
tour.sona.point1: Sona, gallery, projects, links and custom pages
tour.sona.point3: Choose the order and visibility of your menus
tour.audio.title: Set the mood. Keep control.
tour.audio.description: Bring a track you have permission to share. The player loops it across menus and remembers each visitor’s volume and mute settings.
languageBody: The interface follows the browser’s language and remembers a visitor’s choice. Supply your own translations for personal text; names, pronouns and links stay as written.
setupBody: The local setup wizard handles your profile, pages, images and credits. Run it again whenever you want to change something.
updatesBody: Stable GitHub Releases, file verification and backups. If an update conflicts with your edits, the installer stops for a manual merge instead of silently replacing them.

demoBody: Explore a separate sample site, switch languages and try the music controls. It uses demonstration content, not Trim’s personal installation.
demoNote: No account. No configuration is changed on the server. Preferences stay in your browser. The sample audio is an original generated loop.
installIntro: Install Node.js 22 or newer, download the archive, then let the setup wizard guide you. No npm dependencies to install.
runCommand: Run from the extracted project folder
windowsStep1: Download the project ZIP from GitHub Releases.
windowsStep2: Extract the entire archive and open its folder.
windowsStep3: Double-click setup.bat, or run the command below in PowerShell.
windowsStep4: Choose a language and answer the profile questions.
windowsStep5: Choose Preview to open the local address printed by setup.
linuxStep1: Download and extract the ZIP, or clone the repository.
linuxStep2: Open a terminal in the project folder.
linuxStep3: Run bash setup.sh with Node.js 22+ available.
linuxStep4: Choose a language and configure your profile.
linuxStep5: Choose Preview and open the local address printed by setup.
hostNote: Creating a site does not publish it. Export with setup, then host the static files wherever you choose. Never put secrets in a public profile.
sourceTitle: Open source, from the first menu.
sourceBody: Read the code, change your own installation, report a bug or propose an improvement. The code is GPLv3, with the original Trim credit and historical license notices retained.
communityCredit: For creative customizations, a Sona page and ideas for improving the profile.
communityInvite: Built something of your own? Share a link through the project’s GitHub issues.
a1: Yes. The code is free software under GPLv3. Keep Trim’s required attribution and the existing license notices when redistributing it. Nintendo-specific assets have separate notices.
q2: Is this an official Nintendo project?
a2: No. This is an independent fan-made project, without affiliation with or endorsement by Nintendo.
a3: The template and this showcase adapt to smaller screens and touch controls. Chromium desktop and responsive layouts have been tested; support on every physical device or browser is not guaranteed.
q4: Can I use my own music?
a4: Yes. Setup supports MP3, OGG and WAV files, up to 30 MB. You must have the right to share the track. Crediting Nintendo does not grant permission to use its music, and no Nintendo audio is bundled.
q5: Do I need to know how to code?
a5: Not for the usual profile settings. Install Node.js 22+, run setup.bat on Windows or bash setup.sh on Linux, and answer the questions. Hosting your exported site is a separate step explained in the documentation.
a6: The updater separates personal files, makes backups and checks file hashes. Modified core files or personal media conflicts stop the update for a manual merge. Keep your own full backup too; no updater can promise that nothing will ever go wrong.
a7: Yes. Open an issue to explain a bug or discuss an idea, or submit a pull request to the repository. Describe what changed and how you tested it. Community ideas and code contributions are credited separately.
